## People Edit for 8 GB GPUs (e.g. GTX 1080)

FLUX.2 Klein 4B distilled, fp8 weights, 4 steps. Tested under a hard 8 GB VRAM cap: peak ~6.2 GB.
The text encoder (5.4 GB) and the edit model (3.9 GB) take turns on the GPU, so system RAM should be 16 GB or more.

## Prompting tips

- Refer to the inputs as **image 1** (the photo being edited) and **image 2** (the reference: garment, hairstyle, accessory, face...).
- Say what to change **and** what to keep, e.g. *"Keep the face, identity, skin tone, pose, lighting and background unchanged."*
- Be explicit about size and amount (*"shoulder-length"*, *"subtle"*): this smaller model tends to exaggerate edits.
- One or two changes per run work best. For several changes, run again on the output.

## Tradeoffs vs. the Qwen Image 2.1 workflows

- Follows instructions less precisely and slightly less fine detail; identity, pose and background hold up well.
- Inputs are scaled to ~1 megapixel; output follows image 1's aspect ratio.

## Models (in ComfyUI/models)

- diffusion_models/flux-2-klein-4b-fp8.safetensors
- text_encoders/qwen_3_4b_fp8_mixed.safetensors
- vae/flux2-vae.safetensors

## Setting up a GTX 1080 machine

- Pascal (sm_61) needs a PyTorch build for CUDA 12.6 (`--index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126`); CUDA 12.8+/13 builds no longer support it.
- ComfyUI runs fp8 weights on a 1080 by upcasting them to fp16 layer by layer, so no fp8 hardware is needed.
